pl-l4d45c1-d1e115.summary: Quotes Augustine: all souls leaving this world have different receptions, the good joy, the bad torment; but after the resurrection the joy of the good will be greater and the torments of the wicked graver, when they are tormented with the body.
claims: At death souls receive joy or torment.

pl-l4d45c1-d1e124.summary: Draws out that the saints' joy will be greater in and after the resurrection than before, and that the saints' souls will have various dwelling places.
claims: The saints' joy grows at the resurrection.

pl-l4d45c1-d1e127.summary: Cites Augustine: the time between death and the final resurrection holds souls in hidden receptacles, each as worthy of rest or hardship by what it obtained in the flesh while living.
claims: Between death and resurrection souls are held according to their merits.

pl-l4d45c1.summary: All souls on leaving this world have different receptions, the good joy and the bad torment, as Augustine says; after the resurrection the joy of the good and the torments of the wicked will be greater, being shared by the body. Between death and resurrection souls are held in hidden places, at rest or in hardship according to what they merited in the flesh.
claims: Souls receive joy or torment at death.
Joy and torment increase after the resurrection.
Souls are held in hidden places between death and resurrection.
